key_insight: PDI-Bench introduces a single, quantitative Perspective Distortion Index that automatically detects geometric and perspective inconsistencies in generated video clips, providing a diagnostic alternative to subjective human or learned graders.
problem_solved: Existing video-model evaluation relies on subjective human judgments or weakly diagnostic learned graders and lacks standardized, quantitative tests for whether generated videos preserve physically plausible 3D structure and camera-consistent motion.
method: Define a Perspective Distortion Index (PDI) that measures deviations from expected perspective-consistent transformations across frames using geometric cues (e.g., motion/flow, depth cues, and camera pose when available).
Compute framewise and clip-level scores that highlight where and how much perspective distortion occurs, producing interpretable diagnostics rather than a single opaque quality score.
Provide a benchmarked evaluation pipeline to compare models, isolate common geometric failure modes, and produce summary statistics for model auditing.
impact: PDI-Bench gives researchers and engineers a reproducible, diagnostic tool to quantify geometric fidelity in generative video models, enabling better model comparisons, targeted debugging, and training objectives that prioritize physically plausible 3D motion.
visual_elements: Side-by-side frames: real vs. generated with PDI heatmap overlays highlighting distorted regions
Time-series plot of PDI across frames to show where geometric coherence breaks down
Bar chart comparing PDI scores across models/datasets to summarize performance
Schematic diagram showing the geometric cues used (optical flow, depth, camera pose) and how they feed into the PDI computation
paper_title: Quantitative Video World Model Evaluation for Geometric-Consistency
paper_authors: Jiaxin Wu, Yihao Pi, Yinling Zhang, Yuheng Li, Xueyan Zou
